To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the adoption of modern technologies by traditional dairy farmers is stimulated by the availability of modern technologies in the market, but not by vertical coordination in value chain, and that (2) the emergence of a new group of dynamic dairy farms which are fully integrated in value chains is stimulated by the existence of such vertical coordination.

the adoption of modern technologies by dairy farms is crucial for improving productivity and welfare of the poor farmers in developing economies, but that vertical coordination in value chain does not stimulate the adoption of these technologies by the traditional farmers.
the dairy value chain has a positive impact on the adoption of technologies by the traditional dairy farmers but that this impact is not strong.

the role of value chains in stimulating the adoption of modern technology among traditional dairy farmers.
the adoption of technology and value chain development in developing countries and shows how these processes are related.
the role of value chains for technology adoption among traditional farms and the emergence of new dynamic modern dairy farms in Punjab, India.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vertical coordination in value chain does not seem to be an important driver for technology transfer and adoption, but that the emergence of modern value chain participants does.

value chain development in dairy is not a silver bullet for technology adoption in developing country agriculture, but that it is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the development of modern farms.
value chains are important for technology adoption in the modern dairy sector but not in the traditional dairy sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
technology adoption in domestic value chains is a dynamic and complex process which is driven by both traditional and modern dairy farms.
technology adoption and vertical integration are two separate processes in the dairy chain.
technology transfer is a complex process which involves many factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
technology adoption in developing countries is not only a function of the technology itself and the farmer's characteristics, but also of the value chains in which they participate.
vertical coordination in value chain does not necessarily support technology adoption among traditional farmers, but it does support the emergence and growth of modern dairy farms.
value chains do not seem to play a significant role in the adoption of modern technology in domestic food chains.
